title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu tammikuussa – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Urbaria Guest Lecture with Sonja Lakić
content:
This Urbaria Guest lecture is organized in collaboration with , , COMU Research Network, and .

Date: 29 October 2026

Time: 14.15-15.45

Place: F3017, Main Building (Fabianinkatu 33, Helsinki)

Who cares? Lessons on the post-Yugoslav post-socialism: learning about/from Banja Luka (Bosnia and Herzegovina)

Sonja Lakić

Abstract

In this lecture, Sonja Lakić unpacks the post-Yugoslav post-socialism, as exercised in Banja Luka, the second largest city in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the political, administrative, financial, university, and cultural centre of one of the post-war entities of the country, i.e. Republika Srpska.

Alternating between the agencies of an individual, collective, and institutional, Lakić approaches the city as a patchwork of cultures and ideologies, imaginaries and materialities, offering a thorough chronological overview of how (and by whom) Banja Luka has thus-far been curated, as in rewritten, (not) cared for, and/or (not) taken care of.

Bio

Sonja Lakić is a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Institute of Ethnology and Central European and Balkan Studies, Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague, Czech Republic

title: Urbaria Guest Lecture with Professor Matts Hallenberg
content:
Date: 20 October 2026

Time: 14.15-15.15

Place: Seminar room 203, Language Center (Fabianinkatu 26, Helsinki)
 

Title: The Nordic Welfare City: Past, present and future?

Abstract

The expansion of public services was one of the significant markers of modernity. In the nineteenth century, politicians started to invest in systems for sewage, energy and transport, moving on to housing, healthcare and education. The rise of the public was mainly an urban phenomenon, planned and executed by municipal bodies. This also meant a change in the nature of politics: politicians became providers of public goods rather than mere administrators of financial burdens.

How was this historical shift made possible? In our research network we analyse the development of the Nordic Welfare City as a distinct historical phenomenon, preceding the welfare state. I argue that this was due to a new configuration of publicness; a political discourse incorporating conservative, liberal and socialist notions of what the urban community should be.

title: Suomen Metsäsäätiö mukana tukemassa metsä- ja luontoalan innovaatioita
content:
Forest and Nature Tech Pitching Competition is made possible with the support of Finnish Forest Foundation.

Finnish Forest Foundation is a non-profit grant foundation whose purpose is to support the vitality of the forest industry as a cooperation between forest owners, wood buyers and other forest sector actors. The Forest Foundation annually awards grants for projects involving children and young people, research, communication with decision-makers and forest nature. The Forest Foundation operates mainly with donated funds (RA/2023/1002).

Strong innovation ecosystems are built through collaboration. We are delighted to partner with Finnish Forest Foundation, one of the key foundations supporting the forest sector in Finland.

Eight startups and R2B teams participating in the pitching competition have now been announced, and the semifinal will take place next week, on 22 October 2026, at Forest Industry Days.

title: New Nordic project launches to strengthen knowledge on intimate partner homicide
content:
Developing EHM-based Intimate partner homicide monitoring and research system in the Nordic Area, funded by the Nordic Council of Ministers, brings together researchers and experts from Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, the Netherlands and Switzerland.

The project responds to Recommendation 12/2023 of the Nordic Council of Ministers, which calls for uniform definitions and statistics on intimate partner homicide. 

Over the next two years, the project partners will explore how data on intimate partner homicides can be collected and analysed in a more harmonised way across the Nordic region. The work includes a pilot study using the European Homicide Monitor (EHM) framework, which provides a standardized approach for comparing homicide characteristics, patterns and trends across countries and regions.

The project is coordinated by the Institute of Criminology and Legal Policy at the University of Helsinki. It is led by Miisa Törölä and Janne Kivivuori, with Peppiina Heikkilä contributing as project planner.

title: Live-striimit ja yleisölle avoimet tapahtumat Aleksanteri-konferenssissa 2026
content:
The 25th Aleksanteri Conference, entitled “Mapping Security in Central and Eastern Europe and Eurasia: Fault Lines and Frontlines,” brings together the latest research on security and focuses particularly on Eurasia as well as Eastern and Central Europe.The conference programme is partly open to the public and available via live stream. Welcome to follow thought-provoking discussions on security-related topics! The working language of the the conference is English.

Henry E. Hale, Professor at George Washington University, will deliver one of the conference’s keynote addresses at Think Corner (Yliopistonkatu 4) on Thursday, 22 October, from 14:00 to 15:15. The event is open to the public. Hale will explore how Russia’s authoritarian regime appeals to traditional values and why the same strategy that has helped it gain support may ultimately turn against it.

The conference opening (21 October, 10:00-10:45) and closing ceremony (23 October, 14:15-15:00) can be followed via livestream. The keynote speaker at the opening ceremony is Petr Fiala, former Prime Minister of the Czech Republic and Professor at Masaryk University.

title: Tiedemuseoiden yhteiselle hankkeelle Jenny ja Antti Wihurin rahaston apuraha
content:
The Jenny and Antti Wihuri Foundation has awarded €50,000 to Helsinki University Museum Flame and Jyväskylä University Museum for a collaborative project focused on exhibitions and events. This award is a significant boon for the project. Museum directors Miia-Leena Tiili and Pirita Frigren are pleased with the grant: 

“Many thanks to the Wihuri Foundation for your support! This funding enables us to carry out the project components in their planned scope, ensuring high quality and accessibility.”

The university museums are taking several viewpoints on research controversies. Flame will carry out an exhibition exploring rejected methods and ethical missteps in research involving human participants, and also enquiring what is permissible in the name of research. The exhibition at Jyväskylä University Museum examines controversies associated with the collection of scientific specimens. It considers what scientific collections tell us about the evolving relationship between humans and other species, and the role of collections with controversial origins in current research and species protection.
